name: OneSixOne Ventures
identity_check: Confirmed as OneSixOne Ventures (onesixone.ventures), the Gainesville, Florida pre-seed/seed VC co-founded by Justis Mendez and Pablo Casilimas. The firm's team page, its LinkedIn company page and Florida Trend name both as co-founders/managing partners, and the 2022 Form D for ONESIXONE Founders Fund LP lists both as managers of the GP. The Emobi PR Newswire release hyperlinks 'OneSixOne Ventures' to www.onesixone.ventures. The name comes from 1.61 (the golden ratio); press also writes 'One Six One Ventures' (Refresh Miami, Clockout) and '1.61 Ventures' (Nerd Apply release; Nerd Apply is on the firm's own portfolio list). 'ONESIXONE Founders Fund LP' is OneSixOne's own fund vehicle, not Founders Fund (Peter Thiel's firm). The website is a client-rendered app; its text, team, portfolio and Fund II figures were read from the site's JavaScript bundle (/assets/index-Dcp1oPDv.js), which serves every route listed in pages.

open_items: Only 9 rounds recorded, 7 of them from press or company pages. The web-search budget ran out partway through, so more announced rounds probably exist: PitchBook counts 39 investments.

Scholar Education ($2M seed, Sep 2026) and Otto Sales AI ($0.5M seed, Apr 2026) rest on CB Insights and PitchBook only. No press release or company page naming OneSixOne was found, and neither company's website was confirmed. scholar.education is a parked lander, and ottosales.ai matches by name only.

Tandemn and Knowlify come from Florida Trend's description of OneSixOne's 'first check'. No stage or amount was found for OneSixOne's checks. The Tandemn month (2025-06) is PitchBook's fund-profile deal date, and Tandemn's HQ is not stated. knowlify.net now redirects to knowlify.com, which describes an AI-native Meta-ads agency rather than the education-video product the firm and Florida Trend describe.

Leads: no source states whether OneSixOne leads. In every round found it is a participant or 'first check', and in Hedgehog it was 'the smallest check on the cap table' (Refresh Miami). The 'leads' fact is left out.

No portfolio round page naming OneSixOne was found for Hedgehog (investment described by Refresh Miami, Mar 2025; PitchBook deal 01-May-2026), Rain AI ('most recently AI-chips startup RAIN', Refresh Miami, Apr 2024), Betr, Bookster, Gone, Baseline, Textile Labs, Syncurrent, Cospectral, Sunthetics, Mercoa or Cielara AI. The FinSMEs pages for the Sunthetics $4M seed (Nov 2024) and the Rain AI $8.1M Series A extension (May 2024) do not name OneSixOne.

Fund I: the only SEC filing is the 2022 Form D for ONESIXONE Founders Fund LP (indefinite offering, $415,000 sold to 8 investors at filing; Justis Mendez and Pablo Casilimas manage the GP). That this vehicle is 'Fund 1' is inferred from timing and it being the only fund filing. Final size and close date are not published.

Fund II: the site gives a $35M target, pre-seed to seed, $500K-$1.5M checks and 50-60 portfolio companies, and says 'actively raising'. Florida Trend (Feb 2026) says Fund II rolls out 'this year'. No Fund II Form D or close announcement was found; EDGAR company search returns only the Founders Fund LP. The Phase 1 note 'fund closed since the freshness cutoff' is not confirmed by any page; the only 'Closed' status seen is PitchBook's status for the Founders Fund (vintage 2023).

EDGAR now refuses the User-Agent 'CapitalAtlas research' (HTTP 403). The Form D and company-search pages were read earlier in this session with a placeholder example.com contact, not a real person's address.
Nothing found on investing in Indian founders. requires_us_entity is unknown: the site lists a London presence, but nothing says whether a US entity is required.

The site footer reads '© 2025'. Its homepage map shows 13 hubs (Seattle, San Francisco, Austin, Gainesville, Miami, Tampa, Atlanta, Cleveland, Boston, New York City, Los Angeles, Urbana-Champaign and London) under a '12 Cities' heading. These read as event and network hubs, not confirmed offices. agentuity.com now redirects to agentcompany.com.

Partners: the team page also lists Brandon Woodard (Venture Analyst; sports-industry background), omitted as not relevant to industrial / AI / hardware. Partner focus_sectors are inferred from the firm-level AI / cloud-infrastructure focus and Kennamer's IT-infrastructure background; no individual focus is stated.

Despite the Phase 1 'industrial / hard tech / physical AI' label, the portfolio is mostly AI and cloud-infrastructure software, fintech and edtech. No robotics or manufacturing company was found. The closest hardware-adjacent names are Rain AI (neuromorphic chips), Sunthetics (AI for chemical-process R&D), Emobi (EV charging software), EaseAlert (firefighter alert device) and EveryKey (smart key).
